source.title: Keystone metro cost factor (BLS OEWS wages, see README cost method)

factor.note: MSA 15180 Brownsville-Harlingen, TX: labour index L=0.69, materials M=1.0. 5/5 trades (OEWS May 2024 via O*NET Texas local-wages search extracts). Ratios to US: 47-2031 0.620; 47-2111 0.720; 47-2152 0.744; 47-2061 0.699; 49-9021 0.714. L = 0.69; factor = 0.40*0.69 + 0.60*1.00 = 0.88. M=1.00 (default, no public citable reason to adjust).

cost.method: Factor = 0.40*L + 0.60*M, rounded to 2 decimals. L = weighted mean of (metro annual median wage / US national annual median wage) for SOC 47-2031 Carpenters (0.30), 47-2111 Electricians (0.20), 47-2152 Plumbers/Pipefitters/Steamfitters (0.20), 47-2061 Construction Laborers (0.20), 49-9021 HVAC Mechanics/Installers (0.10), from BLS OEWS; weights renormalised over occupations available for the MSA. M = materials index, 1.00 for all Texas metros (no public citable reason to adjust); qualitative materials notes per MSA. Wave 2 (2026-10-11): all five trades retrieved from O*NET Texas local-wages pages (OEWS May 2024) via search extracts (Secondary); HVAC missing for 28660, 47380, 46340, 17780 (weights renormalised there). provisional removed for every MSA with >=4 trades.

plainLanguage: Brownsville is in the Texas windstorm area (TDI treats the city as the old Inland I zone). New homes need TDI windstorm inspections and a WPI-8 certificate; since April 1, 2026 that means the 2024 IRC as adopted by TDI, about 150 mph design wind and impact-rated windows. The common single-family district is R-1: 5,000 sq ft lots, 25 ft front setback (20 ft on a corner side street), small side and rear setbacks and at most 50% lot coverage. Expect a city capital recovery fee of about $850-$1,050 per home plus BPUB utility impact fees. We could not confirm which IRC edition the city itself has adopted or its flood freeboard, so check with the city before building.
